quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to drive, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Encourage other friends to talk them out of driving.
Tell them to use less-crowded roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: You can help prevent drunk driving in many ways. Arrange other transportation, keep them busy to slow their drinking, use an excuse to keep them from leaving, or ask other friends to help stop them. These actions are good. Suggesting they take less-crowded roads is not helpful.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders together.
Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
Move only your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn just your head, keep your shoulders still, and look straight ahead.

questions.question: An integrated braking system:

options.text: Uses the rear brake to help apply the front brake.
Uses the front brake to help apply the rear brake.
Applies equal braking to both front and rear when either brake is used.
Remembers how hard you brake and learns your style.

questions.correctAnswerText: Uses the front brake to help apply the rear brake.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system applies some front braking whenever you use the rear brake. This helps slow the motorcycle. Check your motorcycle's owner's manual for details about your specific braking system.

questions.question: A child passenger should:

options.text: Sit in front of the driver.
Not need to reach the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit behind the driver.
questions.explanation: A child should always sit right behind the driver. If a child sits in front, they may not balance well and could get in the way of the driver's controls.

questions.question: Wearing a helmet makes you ________ more likely to survive a crash than not wearing one.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: At any speed, wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a head injury in a crash.

questions.question: When braking on a wet or slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Not brake, but shift to a lower gear instead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: On wet or slippery surfaces, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes gently if you need to stop.

questions.question: Small vehicles can look ______ away and seem to be going ______ than they really are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther, slower
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can look farther away and seem slower than they actually are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge their real location and speed.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.
Slow down as you approach, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If chased by a dog, shift to a lower gear and approach slowly. Then speed up and leave the dog behind.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Squeeze the front brake hard to keep the tire from locking.
Use only one brake at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to stop. Squeeze the brake lever slowly to avoid locking the front wheel, and use gentle pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?
questions.correctAnswerText: Once a week
questions.explanation: Before every ride, inspect your motorcycle for safety. Check hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week.

questions.question: A helmet should NOT:

options.text: Have been worn in an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have been worn in an accident.
questions.explanation: A good helmet meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly, and has no obvious defects. If a helmet was worn during a crash, replace it.

questions.question: To prevent fatigue on a long ride, you should do all of the following, EXCEPT:

options.text: Limit how far you ride in a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take artificial stimulants.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue, dress for bad weather, limit riding to about six hours per day, and take a break every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants because extreme fatigue may occur when they wear off.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn just your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right turn
questions.explanation: A left arm bent at the elbow and pointing upward means you plan to turn right or change lanes to the right. Use hand signals instead of or along with turn signals.

questions.question: A larger cushion of space may not be necessary if:

options.text: You cannot see through the vehicle ahead of you.
Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when conditions are bad. You need extra space if the pavement is slippery, you cannot see ahead, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Avoid placing you in other drivers' blind spots.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Provide you with an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see others, avoids blind spots, keeps you away from wind blasts and hazards, discourages other drivers from sharing your lane, and gives you an escape route.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center portion of the lane.
Stay in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind or from oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane. Moving toward the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: Fatigue can be increased by:

options.text: Starting a ride late in the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in cool weather.
questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from tiring weather like wind and rain. Limit riding to about six hours per day and take breaks every two hours. Avoid artificial stimulants because extreme fatigue can occur when they wear off.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of the lane should you usually use?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
Either the left or right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you farthest from opening doors, people stepping out, and cars pulling out.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks that run parallel to the road, you should:

options.text: Cross the tracks at a 90-degree angle.
Avoid crossing the tracks for any reason.
Cross the tracks at at least a 45-degree angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the tracks at at least a 45-degree angle.
questions.explanation: Cross railroad tracks, trolley tracks, or pavement seams at an angle of at least 45 degrees with a quick, sharp turn. Edging across slowly can catch your tire and throw you off balance.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another driver on the left, you should:

options.text: Move to the right side of your lane so they can see you in their side mirror.
Move to the left side of your lane so you can see better.
Stay in the center of your lane so they can see you in their rearview mirror.
Weave in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the left side of your lane so you can see better.
questions.explanation: When passing another vehicle on the left, stay in the left part of your lane. This helps you see better and makes you more visible to other drivers. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: Look through turns toward where you want to go. Turn only your head to look, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what following distance should you maintain?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead of you under normal conditions. Increase this distance if weather is bad, visibility is poor, or roads are wet.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, slow down and approach it. Then speed up and ride away. If you see a larger animal, brake and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the alcohol is consumed
How often the drinker consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the drinker consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: Three things affect BAC: how much alcohol is consumed, how fast it is consumed, and body weight. How often someone drinks does not affect their BAC. Never drive after drinking alcohol.
